baseline.name: Recursive construction reusing one half-order
baseline.approach: Recursively compute one beautiful half-order of size ceil(n/2) once, then reuse that order to emit the bounded odd and even mappings. Do not make two independent recursive subcalls.
baseline.space: O(n) total arrays plus O(log n) recursion depth

archived.name: Iterative odd/even expansion
archived.space: O(n) temporary buffer plus O(n) output

why: The archive flattens the same parity-preserving construction into buffer passes and avoids recursive calls.
quantitative_comparison: Expansion lengths double until n, so the sum of processed lengths is O(n). The recursive baseline can also have O(n) total work and storage; removing logarithmic call depth does not establish a better dominant bound or measured speed.
tradeoffs: Two n-element buffers are reserved, n must be positive, and a partial allocation failure leaks the other successful allocation. No general better-performance claim is established.
evidence_basis: Static comparison of equivalent constructive recurrences; no timing benchmark.
